correctness.rationale: For each complete cycle the normalized pre-reset energy is exactly (1-U)Z²/2 with U~Beta(beta,1) independent of the standard Gaussian Z, beta=r/(2mu). The full conditional-Gaussian derivation in RESULT.md fixes constants and hypotheses. Substitution v=wu in the exact erfc integral has an explicit integrable beta*v^(beta-1)*exp(-v) bound and yields both the sharp tail and conditional Gamma mark. The sharp tail and iid cycles imply a Gumbel maximum; joint rare marked probabilities and binomial-to-Poisson convergence yield independent Gumbel and Gamma limits, giving age ~loglog n/(2mu). Exponential-moment finiteness at s=1 is the beta integral beta∫u^(beta-3/2)du, finite iff r>mu. Gaussian marks indexed by longest reset duration remain standard normal, proving their energy is tight while the maximum diverges. Standalone verify.py executed successfully with 88 finite numerical checks, and is supplementary rather than proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 harmonic resetting heat-engine study motivates studying rare per-reset energetic displacements rather than mean energetic cycles. The joint law identifies which reset intervals produce the largest harmonic energy and proves their durations are doubly logarithmic, fundamentally shorter than the exponential-clock longest interval. The precise Gamma age mark, exact Gumbel centering, sharp tail constant and critical reset-to-relaxation threshold for the exponential moment are natural observables for rare reset-energy events. This is not a tiny parameter improvement or a mere stationary-density recomputation, and explicitly excludes model-dependent physical work.
